parent_id.description: Containment parent id; null on turns and session-level out-of-band nodes.

refs.description: Non-containment node/session references. Local node ids are graph-scoped; session references use explicit session ids.

node.parent_id: str | null  (null on a turn or session-level out-of-band node; roots is the ordered turn index)
node.refs: dict  (non-containment node/session references; local node ids or explicit session ids)

assistant.description: One API response. Claude Code splits a response across several transcript records; they are collapsed to one node here, so one node is one billable response.

attribution_agent.description: The agent type this response was produced by — `general-purpose`, `Explore`, a named custom agent. Non-null only on a subagent stream, so it is null throughout a master session. Not the same as `spawn.agent_type`, which is what the parent *requested*; this is what the running side reports.

attribution_plugin.description: The plugin supplying the active skill. Looks like the prefix of `attribution_skill` (`superpowers:…`) and is carried separately anyway — the two are not in exact correspondence (3,601 vs 3,879 records in the measured corpus), so deriving one from the other would be a guess.

attribution_skill.description: The skill whose instructions were in force for this response, as the harness stamped it — e.g. `my-arch-doc`, `superpowers:writing-plans`. Null when none was active. This is what the response actually ran under, which the `skill_listing` attachment cannot tell you: that only says what was offered in context.

cache_write_tokens.description: Tokens written to cache, all TTLs.

effort.description: The reasoning-effort level the response ran at, when the vendor reported one. Null when unreported — which is not the same as low effort.

estimated_reasoning_tokens.description: Reasoning recovered by subtraction: `output_tokens` minus the counted visible output minus per-tool-call framing. **Inside `output_tokens`, not on top of it** — summing both double counts. An estimate unless `reasoning_source` says `reported`. See docs/design/notes/claude_token_usage.md.

estimated_visible_tokens.description: Raw tokenizer count of the visible output — reply text plus tool names and arguments, reasoning excluded. Stored unconverted so a ratio change re-derives from the graph without re-running the normalizer.

has_thinking.description: Whether the model reasoned here. The reasoning text itself is stripped by Claude Code before the transcript is written, so this flag plus the token estimate below is all that survives.

input_tokens.description: Tokens sent. From the response's settled usage, not a per-record partial.

message_id.description: The API response id. Several transcript records share it; this node is their collapse, so the id is also the node's identity.

model.description: Model that produced the response. Subagents routinely differ from the parent.

output_tokens.description: Tokens produced, **including reasoning** — it is billed here and never broken out separately by the vendor.

reasoning_ratio.description: The tokenizer ratio applied to reach the estimate: 1.52 for the Claude 5 family, 1.13 for Sonnet 4.6. **1.0 means the model was not measured** and the raw tokenizer count was used unconverted, making the estimate an upper bound.

reasoning_source.description: `reported` when the vendor published a reasoning count (Codex does today, Claude may later) — then no estimation ran. `estimated` when it was derived.

tool_call_count.description: Tool-use blocks in this response. Each costs a fixed block of output tokens beyond its arguments, which is why the reasoning estimate needs the count.

spawn.description: A subagent delegation. Exactly two tool names become one — `Agent` and `Task`; every other tool stays a `tool` node. `TaskCreate`/`TaskUpdate` are todo-list bookkeeping and delegate nothing, despite the name. The subagent's work is in a *separate* graph, reached through `refs.child_session_id`; nothing about the child is inlined here.

agent_type.description: Which agent was asked for, e.g. `Explore`, `general-purpose`.

description.description: Short task label recorded when the subagent was spawned; it is not the full delegated instruction.

duration_ms.description: Child duration recorded with the spawn event, when supplied; it is not calculated from a loaded child graph.

prompt_char_count.description: Length of the spawn instruction before scrubbing. The instruction content is not repeated here.

requested_model.description: Model requested for the child at spawn time, when the producer supplied one.

resolved_model.description: Model the child actually used, which routinely differs from both the request and the parent — so a subagent's cost cannot be assumed from the parent's.

result.description: The delegation's outcome, in the same facet-grouped shape as a tool node's `result` — see `tool.result`. Only the `delegation` facet is expected here in practice: `agent_id`, `prompt` (the full delegated instruction — the one place it survives; the call side only ever carries its character count), `duration_ms`, `tool_use_count`, `tool_stats`, and, for a delegation still running when its parent read the result, `is_async`/`output_file`/`can_read_output_file` in place of the duration/count fields. `agent_type`/`status`/`resolved_model` are not repeated here — they are already this node's own attrs, from the call side.

run_in_background.description: Whether the parent continued without waiting for the child, when supplied by the spawn event.

status.description: Outcome once the child finished. Null while it is still running.

tool.description: One tool invocation merged with its result, so a node carries both what was asked and what happened. Tools under one assistant are an unordered set — they share a `message_id` and nothing sequences them.

blocked_on_user_ms.description: Time spent waiting for a human to approve the call. OTEL-only; always null in a graph built from JSONL, which has no equivalent.

cmd.description: Ordered executable basenames extracted from configured shell-capable tool input. Empty for non-shell tools or failed command parsing; repeated commands are retained.

duration_ms.description: How long the tool took. Frequently null even on success — only present when the vendor happened to report it.

exit_status.description: Process exit status, for tools that run commands.

file_change.description: True when this call touched files. `select(type='file_change')` matches on it — files are carried on tool nodes, there is no separate file node type.

memory_access.description: Present and true only when at least one file on this Tool matches the ordered memory-classifier rules for the graph vendor. It is a query selection marker; classification details remain on each matching files[] entry.

files.description: One entry per file touched: `path`, `extension`, `artifact_class`, `operation`, `hunks`, plus `is_memory:true` and `memory_kind:index|entry|unknown` only when the reported path matches the configured harness memory classifier. Reach into it with a `files[].field` path — e.g. `where {"files[].extension": ".md"}` — since none of it is top-level.

input.description: The arguments the model generated, verbatim and vendor-shaped. Generated file content is scrubbed upstream when configured.

is_error.description: Whether the tool reported failure. From the paired result, not the call.

result.description: The tool's outcome beyond pass/fail, extracted from the vendor's raw result into vendor-neutral facets — `process` (Bash stdout/stderr), `git` (a durable git action the vendor flagged: commit/push/pr/branch), `file` (Read/Write/Edit facts not already on `files[]` — no `path`, no `hunks`, those live there), `interaction` (AskUserQuestion), `web` (WebFetch/WebSearch), `todo` (TaskCreate/Update/List), `skill` (Skill), `search` (ToolSearch), `worktree` (Enter/ExitWorktree), `message` (SendMessage), `findings` (ReportFindings), `monitor` (Monitor), `exit_plan_mode` (the ExitPlanMode tool — not plan mode, see `turn.plan_mode`), and `mcp` (any `mcp__*` tool, resolved through the vendor's parsed carrier when present). Always carries `outcome` (`ok`/`error`/`denied`) and `error_text` (the bare-string result on failure, else null); every other facet is present only when applicable — never an empty object. `result.unmapped` holds any vendor key no facet claimed, verbatim, so nothing is silently dropped as the vendor's shape drifts. Absent entirely, not an empty object, when the call has no result at all.

tool_denial_kind.description: Why a call was refused, when it was: the user declined, a permission rule blocked it. Null when the call was not denied.

tool_name.description: The tool as the model named it, e.g. `Bash`, `Edit`, `Read`. Note `TaskCreate`/`TaskUpdate` appear here and are todo-list bookkeeping, not subagent delegation — only `Agent`/`Task` become `spawn` nodes.

turn.description: One `promptId` run: a user prompt and everything the agent did before the next prompt. Turns are the graph's roots — they have no parent node, which is why two nodes in different turns have no containment path between them. The canonical identity is **`{session_id, turn_num}`**. Inside one session the local node `id` is `"turn:{turn_num}"`; `attrs.turn_num` is the same 1-based sequence number. `attrs.prompt_id` is retained only as vendor provenance and is never identity. Every family-wide index also scopes non-turn local ids by `session_id`, because sibling agent graphs may legitimately reuse any local id. A compaction does not add a turn or renumber one here — it is a separate `compaction` node, and the turns it relates carry `is_after_compact` / `triggered_compaction`. **Known limit:** `turn_num` is positional — stable across a rebuild of the same transcript, but if the vendor itself rewrites earlier history the positions shift.

attribution.description: Which skill, plugin, agent and effort level produced the work under this turn — the distinct non-null values of the assistants beneath it, as `{skill, plugin, agent, effort}`. **Every field is always a list**, `[]` when nothing was attributed: never a scalar, never null, so a consumer needs one code path rather than a type check. Order is first-seen. Nested rather than flat for the same reason `tokens` is — a turn carrying `attribution_skill` beside an assistant's identically named field invites reading one for the other. **Containment only**: a subagent's attribution stays in the child graph.

duration_ms.description: Wall-clock for the turn. Never null: taken from the vendor's `turn_duration` record, else OTEL's `interaction.duration_ms`, else last-event minus start.

permission_mode.description: The permission mode the turn's opening prompt was sent under — `auto`, `plan`, `acceptEdits`, `default`. **Null, not a default**, when the vendor recorded no mode (245 of 584 turns in the measured corpus, all from older agent versions): unknown and a particular mode are different claims. Stamped once per prompt — no tool result carries one — so there is no mid-turn mode change to read.

plan_mode.description: True when this turn ran in plan mode — `permission_mode == 'plan'`, kept separately because "was this planning or doing" is the common filter. Null, not false, when no mode was recorded. A *planning episode* spans several turns and is not stored: it is a run of consecutive turns with `plan_mode` true, closed by an accepted `ExitPlanMode` (see `tool.result.exit_plan_mode`) or by nothing at all — 5 of 10 runs in the corpus ended without one.

prompt_id.description: The vendor's `promptId` for this turn, unchanged, queryable — but **not the turn's identity**. It is provenance for correlation with a raw transcript; identity is `{session_id, turn_num}`.

status.description: `completed` (a close marker was seen), `interrupted` (work happened, no close marker — the session was cut off), or `empty` (a prompt with no work after it).

tokens.description: Usage of every assistant **beneath this turn**, summed at build time: `input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, `cache_read_tokens`, `cache_write_tokens`, `estimated_reasoning_tokens`. Nested rather than flat on purpose — a turn carrying `output_tokens` beside an assistant's identically named field invites summing both and double counting the session. **Containment only**: tokens spent by subagents this turn spawned are not included, because they live in a separate graph. `budget(by='turn')` is the figure that walks the spawn edge and includes them; this is the turn's own cost.

turn_num.description: The 1-based position of this turn within its session. Together with the graph's `session_id` it is the canonical turn identity. The local node `id` is derived as `turn:{turn_num}`.

is_after_compact.description: Present and `true` only on a turn that resumed after a context compaction — its `isCompactSummary` message descends from a compaction node listed in `refs.resumed_from_compaction_ids`. Absent (not `false`) on an ordinary turn. Named vendor-neutrally rather than after the vendor's `isCompactSummary` flag, since another vendor may signal a resume differently.

triggered_compaction.description: Present and `true` only on the turn whose context growth triggered an **auto** compaction, resolved from the compaction's preserved pre-compaction tail; `refs.triggered_compaction_ids` links every such node. Absent on every other turn — a user-initiated (`manual`) compaction is unrelated to any turn and marks none. For a mid-turn auto compaction this is the same turn that also carries `is_after_compact`.

compaction.description: A context compaction: the harness paused the conversation, summarized it with a dedicated API call, and resumed with a smaller context. **Not part of any turn** — it is a session-level out-of-band node with no containment parent and is not in `roots` (the ordered turn index). It is found by type or through non-containment `refs`: `refs.resumed_turn_id` (the turn that continued after it, also flagged `turn.is_after_compact`) and, for an `auto` compaction only, `refs.triggering_turn_id` (the turn whose growth triggered it, also flagged `turn.triggered_compaction`). Its summarization-call usage is not recoverable here — see `usage_known`.

trigger.description: `auto` (the harness compacted because the context hit its limit) or `manual` (a user-initiated `/compact`). Only an `auto` compaction is attributed to a triggering turn — see `turn.triggered_compaction`.

tokens_before.description: Context size just before the compaction, from the vendor's `compactMetadata` — the size that tripped the limit. **A context size, not this call's input tokens**: the summarization request's own usage is absent from the JSONL (`usage_known`).

tokens_after.description: Context size the session resumed with, from `compactMetadata`.

tokens_reclaimed.description: `tokens_before - tokens_after` — how much context the compaction freed. A waste/efficiency signal, not a billed amount.

duration_ms.description: Wall-clock the harness spent compacting, from `compactMetadata`. This is the pause the summarization call cost in time, not its token cost.

usage_known.description: Always `false` for JSONL. The compaction is a dedicated Claude API request whose own token usage is **not** recorded in the JSONL, so its cost cannot be attributed from this source; the `tokens_*` fields are context sizes, not the call's usage (issue #40). The flag names the missing fact directly so a consumer never reads the deltas as usage or cost.

user_prompt.description: The instruction that opened a turn. In a subagent graph this is the parent's delegation, not something a person typed — `is_injected` tells them apart.

is_injected.description: **True means the harness produced this, not a person** — a skill body, a system reminder, a task notification, a subagent's delegated instruction. Filter on it before treating a prompt as something a human asked for.

model.description: Model named in the prompt record; usually null, the assistant carries it.

resources.description: Ids of `attachment` events in context for this turn — pointers, not copies. The attachment bodies live in the normalized events, not in the graph.

text.description: The instruction, uncapped. Prompts are the primary intent signal, so unlike every other content field they are never truncated.
